body.statement: For the isolated-bow baseline, \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=1,S_b=1)=1/12\), \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=0,S_b=1)=1/24\), and \(P_{\sigma}(S_b=1)=1/2\), so the two full selected observational laws agree. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_b=0)\), the unselected outcome probabilities are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), the selection normalizers are \(25/48\) and \(23/48\), the joint numerators at \(Y_b=C_b=1\) are \(9/25\) and \(7/23\), and the conditional effects are \(18/25\) and \(14/23\). However \(D_{\rho}=1/2\) in both models solely because \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root. This proposition is a vacuous-denominator regression baseline and supplies no evidence for generic denominator locking.
body.justification: Keeping the exact calculation visible prevents a structurally automatic denominator from being mistaken for evidence about informative conditioning.
body.gap: The baseline was previously used as support for denominator locking even though isolation makes the denominator equality automatic.
body.consumer: Certificate tests must classify this example as numerically valid but noninformative about the open graph-to-lock step.
